superpowers.note: Strong design with a testable statusUpdater seam and debug-to-stderr fix, but misses that the repo does not compile (duplicate FormatComments), so its TDD and E2E steps would fail at the start.

code-design.note: Catches the duplicate FormatComments build break, gives a numbered call chain with per-step errors, a data table and explicit assumptions, though runTasksStatus is left untested.

feature-dev.note: Also catches the build break and adds SetBaseURL and command-level test seams, but adds unrequested scope (no-arg listing, JSON modes, output helpers) that makes the plan heavier.

plain.note: Concise and mostly accurate, but misses the compile error, leaves the test seam for the commands package as an open hint, and has thinner failure-path design.

reason: X and Y alone found that the repository does not build (FormatComments declared twice in internal/output/table.go, confirmed with go build), which any implementation session would hit first; X wins by keeping scope to the request while laying out the call chain, per-step errors and assumptions precisely. Y is equally correct but broader than asked, W has the best test seam but ignores the build failure, and Z is the thinnest.
